title: Next year’s Eurovision host is Burgas, not Sofia. Some Bulgarians are baffled
excerpt: Next year’s competition won’t take place in the country’s capital, an announcement that even surprised Bulgarian winner, Dara
content_html:
Ever since Bulgarian singer Dara was crowned winner of the Eurovision song contest this May, it has been clear that the Balkan nation would for the first time in its history have the opportunity to host Europe’s biggest party.

So when Bulgarian officials announced last week that the world’s largest live music event in 2027 will be held not in the capital Sofia but in Burgas, a Black Sea port city home to 200,000 people, it came as a surprise – even to last year’s winner.

“I am really surprised,” singer Dara told the Guardian. “I think that BNT [Bulgarian National Television] will do a great job at producing the whole show. I trust them completely. If they decided Burgas, then probably Burgas is better.”

This spring in Vienna, Dara became the first Bulgarian to win Eurovision with her high energy party anthem Bangaranga, in an edition boycotted by Ireland, Spain, the Netherlands, Slovenia and Iceland over Israel’s participation.

Following her victory, Bulgaria’s four largest cities, Sofia, Plovdiv, Dara’s home town of Varna and Burgas sent an application with only Sofia and Burgas left as possible candidates in recent weeks. As the country’s capital and international hub, Sofia always seemed the obvious choice.

The preference for Burgas, Bulgaria’s fourth largest city, has been heavily discussed across the Balkan country of 6.5 million people, with many taken aback.

“We were surprised, because Sofia has the biggest arena,” said Pavel Stefanov, 29, an air traffic controller at Sofia airport.

Milena Ouzounova, 54, a designer from Sofia said she was surprised and disappointed that the capital wasn’t chosen as host city and was sceptical over Burgas’ capacity to pull off such an event.

“I’m disappointed,” she said. “I think Sofia is a better place, it is bigger, we have a big arena. Burgas is a nice place but I am not sure it could be prepared enough after one year. I think the space is much smaller in Burgas.”

Located on the southern Black Sea coast, approximately 400km east of Sofia, Burgas is closer in distance to Istanbul than the Bulgarian capital.

Nestled among three lakes and the Black Sea, it has an established tourism industry and is a popular seaside destination among Bulgarian and international tourists. Meanwhile, it is home to Bulgaria’s second largest port and the largest oil refinery in southern Europe, accounting for a considerable chunk of the city’s industrial production.

Earlier this year, it hosted the arrival of the first stage of the 2026 Giro d’Italia, the Italian equivalent to the Tour de France, and hosting Eurovision will most likely boost Burgas candidacy for European Capital of Culture in 2032.

Preparations to host the Eurovision grand final have already started around Arena Burgas, the 15,000 concert capacity hall completed in 2023 which will have the herculean task of throwing Europe’s favourite party, while the city’s airport said it is ready to welcome the increased passenger flow for Eurovision 2027.

The accompanying Eurovision events will be in the centre of Burgas and the Sea Garden, the city’s biggest public park directly facing the Black Sea, where locals usually gather to hang out or have a drink.

However, it isn’t the smallest city to ever arrange Eurovision, still considerably bigger than Harrogate, which hosted it in 1982 following Bucks Fizz’s victory.

The Eurovision final will take place on 15 May, with the semi-finals on 11 and 13 May and will have Canada participating for the first time. Meanwhile new rules will be implemented such as increasing the minimum participation age from 16 to 18 and potentially barring countries involved in armed conflicts from hosting.

Many in Bulgaria believe this to be the perfect opportunity to showcase the beauty of the Bulgarian coast and boost tourism, while others are thankful it won’t be organised in Sofia.

Dimitar Nikolov, mayor of Burgas, said he was honoured that Burgas was chosen and thanked BNT and the EBU [European Broadcasting Union] “for the unique chance to present the beauties of Bulgaria and, through Burgas, to all the guests and fans who will follow the live broadcast to feel Bulgaria.”

Prime minister Rumen Radev told local reporters that he believed Burgas will succeed in representing Bulgaria with dignity.

“I think that every Bulgarian city has something to offer both in terms of culture and history, especially in terms of people and modern services. So let’s present ourselves with dignity. I think that Burgas is a really good choice,” he said.

Katrin Ninova, 20, a data science student at the Sofia University said she was relieved that Sofia will avoid Eurovision mayhem. “It’s crowded enough here. We don’t need to organise Eurovision,” she said.

Evtim Vodenicharov, 32, a data manager from Burgas said he was thrilled that his home town would be organising the event and believed that it will boost the region’s economy and tourism. Meanwhile, he hopes to attend next year’s Eurovision in the arena.

“Of course I’m excited,” said Vodenicharov. “I hope I will be able to get a ticket and go watch it live instead of being at home and watching it on TV. It’s in my home town.”

Meanwhile Dara urged visitors who will attend Eurovision to take the opportunity to visit Bulgaria, the Black Sea coast and discover the unique culture of the Balkan country.

“We should look at all of the positive sides. I think people should go to the seaside and all around Burgas, there are really good places,” she said.

content_html_zh:
自从保加利亚歌手达拉今年五月荣获欧洲歌唱大赛冠军以来，很明显这个巴尔干国家将在其历史上第一次有机会举办欧洲最大的派对。

因此，当保加利亚官员上周宣布 2027 年世界上最大的现场音乐活动将不是在首都索非亚举行，而是在拥有 20 万人口的黑海港口城市布尔加斯举行时，即使是去年的获胜者也感到惊讶。

“我真的很惊讶，”歌手达拉告诉卫报。 “我认为 BNT（保加利亚国家电视台）在制作整个节目方面会做得很好。 我完全信任他们。 如果他们选择布尔加斯，那么布尔加斯可能会更好。”

今年春天，达拉在维也纳凭借充满活力的党歌《Bangaranga》成为第一位赢得欧洲歌唱大赛冠军的保加利亚人，而爱尔兰、西班牙、荷兰、斯洛文尼亚和冰岛因以色列的参赛而抵制该版本。

在她获胜后，保加利亚四个最大的城市索非亚、普罗夫迪夫、达拉的家乡瓦尔纳和布尔加斯发出了申请，最近几周只剩下索非亚和布尔加斯作为可能的候选人。 作为该国的首都和国际中心，索非亚似乎总是显而易见的选择。

对于保加利亚第四大城市布尔加斯的青睐，在这个拥有 650 万人口的巴尔干国家引起了热烈讨论，许多人都感到惊讶。

“我们很惊讶，因为索非亚拥有最大的竞技场，”29 岁的索非亚机场空中交通管制员帕维尔·斯特凡诺夫 (Pavel Stefanov) 说。

54 岁的索非亚设计师 Milena Ouzounova 表示，她对首都没有被选为主办城市感到惊讶和失望，并对布尔加斯举办此类活动的能力表示怀疑。

“我很失望，”她说。 “我认为索非亚是一个更好的地方，它更大，我们有一个很大的竞技场。 布尔加斯是一个不错的地方，但我不确定一年后它是否能做好充分的准备。 我认为布尔加斯的空间要小得多。”

布尔加斯位于黑海南部海岸，索非亚以东约 400 公里处，距离伊斯坦布尔比保加利亚首都更近。

它坐落在三个湖泊和黑海之间，拥有成熟的旅游业，是保加利亚和国际游客中受欢迎的海滨目的地。 同时，它还是保加利亚第二大港口和南欧最大炼油厂的所在地，占该市工业生产的相当大一部分。

今年早些时候，布尔加斯举办了 2026 年环意自行车赛（相当于意大利环法自行车赛）第一赛段的举办，而举办欧洲电视网很可能会提高布尔加斯 2032 年欧洲文化之都的候选资格。

举办欧洲歌唱大赛总决赛的准备工作已经在布尔加斯竞技场周围开始，这座可容纳 15,000 人的音乐厅于 2023 年竣工，将承担举办欧洲最受欢迎的派对的艰巨任务，而该市机场表示已准备好迎接 2027 年欧洲歌唱大赛增加的客流量。

伴随的欧洲歌唱大赛活动将在布尔加斯市中心和海洋花园举行，这是该市最大的公园，直接面向黑海，当地人通常聚集在那里闲逛或喝一杯。

然而，它并不是举办欧洲歌唱大赛的最小城市，仍然比哈罗盖特大得多，哈罗盖特于 1982 年雄鹿队 (Bucks Fizz) 获胜后主办了欧洲歌唱大赛。

欧洲歌唱大赛决赛将于5月15日举行，半决赛将于5月11日至13日举行，加拿大将首次参赛。 与此同时，新规则将实施，例如将最低参与年龄从 16 岁提高到 18 岁，并可能禁止卷入武装冲突的国家主办。

许多保加利亚人认为这是展示保加利亚海岸美景和促进旅游业发展的绝佳机会，而另一些人则庆幸这次活动不会在索非亚举办。

布尔加斯市市长迪米塔尔·尼科洛夫 (Dimitar Nikolov) 表示，他很荣幸布尔加斯被选中，并感谢 BNT 和 EBU（欧洲广播联盟）“提供了独特的机会来展示保加利亚的美丽，并通过布尔加斯向所有关注直播的嘉宾和球迷展示保加利亚的魅力。”

总理鲁门·拉德夫告诉当地记者，他相信布尔加斯将成功地有尊严地代表保加利亚。

“我认为每个保加利亚城市在文化和历史方面都有所贡献，特别是在人民和现代服务方面。 因此，让我们有尊严地展示自己。 我认为布尔加斯是一个非常好的选择，”他说。

20 岁的索非亚大学数据科学专业学生卡特琳·尼诺娃 (Katrin Ninova) 表示，索非亚能够避免欧洲歌唱大赛的混乱，让她感到欣慰。 “这里已经够拥挤了。 我们不需要组织欧洲歌唱大赛，”她说。

32 岁的布尔加斯数据经理 Evtim Vodenicharov 表示，他很高兴家乡能够组织这次活动，并相信这将促进该地区的经济和旅游业。 同时，他希望能够在赛场上参加明年的欧洲歌唱大赛。

“我当然很兴奋，”沃杰尼察洛夫说。 “我希望我能够买到票并去看现场直播，而不是在家看电视。 这是在我的家乡。”

同时，达拉敦促将参加欧洲歌唱大赛的观众抓住机会参观保加利亚、黑海沿岸，探索巴尔干国家的独特文化。

“我们应该看到所有积极的一面。 我认为人们应该去海边和布尔加斯周围，那里确实有很多好地方，”她说。
